Abstract says attacks should be evaluated by TPR at low (e.g. <0.1%) FPR. Record's extra clause that a near-0.5 AUC can hide a few confidently identified records is the paper's general argument against average-case metrics but not an abstract statement; it is not claimed as a quote.
pip docs: 'Hashes are required for all dependencies' and an unhashed/unlisted dependency results in an error. Supports record's lock-files-with-hashes prevention item.
SRE book lists on-call intervention (release rollback, rerouting of traffic, etc.) among common postmortem triggers; matches record's 'typical postmortem trigger'.
Embracing Risk: difference between SLO and measured uptime is the budget; releases can be pushed while budget remains and are temporarily halted when it is used up. Matches.

Page: blameless postmortem assumes everyone had good intentions; monitoring failure (usually manual discovery) is a listed trigger. 'Fix systems and processes' is the page's blameless theme; matches record.

Paper lists 'Dependency changes result in notification' (Monitor 1) and 'Models are tested via a canary process before they enter production serving environments' (Infra 6). Record's description matches.
MLflow docs: 'prompt versions are immutable once created'; alias described as a mutable named reference. Matches record.

SRE workbook: 'It should be sizeable and last long enough to be representative of the overall deployment.' Record's follow-on clause that a slow outcome metric 'can never' satisfy this is the author's inference, not the source's; hedged below.

note: Spotify Confidence: SRM p-value threshold typically 0.001, deliberately strict to avoid false alarms; do not interpret results until the imbalance is investigated and resolved. Matches record's 'many teams use something like 0.001' (source speaks for Confidence's own default).
Rule #29 recommends saving serving-time features and states doing it for a small fraction is worthwhile (framed as enabling verification of train/serve consistency, which fits the record's use).

Paper does present 28 tests and monitoring needs, and includes training/serving skew ('compute the same values') and prediction-quality regression. But no monitoring test is about prediction distributions, and model staleness (Monitor 4, also feature-table age) is not generically 'freshness checks'. Record's 'prediction-distribution and freshness checks, which the ML Test Score lists' overreaches.
narrowed_supports: Presents 28 specific tests and monitoring needs, including monitoring tests for training/serving feature consistency, model staleness and prediction-quality regression.
